html:
SMTO-CTX-0040 — The task tried to update a summary of an earlier stage

GUID: 5d32bb86-d1f8-5281-b607-6fa2549d53c3
Slug: task-context-epoch-closed
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: task-context

What happened

  • Long tasks are split into stages, and each stage gets a short summary. The task tried to write a summary for a stage that has already closed, so SMTO refused. Earlier summaries stay as they were.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task continue and watch its activity for a summary written to the current stage. Only the current stage accepts a new summary, and the task can switch to it on its own.
  2. If the task keeps repeating this message, select Steer and ask it to summarize only its current progress. Summaries of closed stages can't be changed, so retrying that won't work.

What success looks like

  • The task saves its current summary and continues working.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to edit earlier summaries; they are kept as a fixed record of finished stages.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Task Context summary write targeted an epoch that is no longer current; only the current epoch accepts a summary (epoch_closed).

What this means

  • A summary write targets an epoch that is no longer current. The recorded reason and operation message identify the specific condition.

Why this can happen

  • The notebook write targets an epoch that no longer accepts changes.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the operation, reason, revision and source reference recorded by the producer.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the current epoch in Task Context and write the summary for that epoch only; historical epochs are read-only. Do not try to bypass the closed-epoch check or overwrite an earlier summary.
  • Inspect the current epoch and write its summary. Historical epochs cannot accept new summaries.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the indicated argument or refresh the source first; retain existing access checks and revision checks.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected notebook operation succeeds.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass source access checks or overwrite a revision conflict.

Technical notes

  • An unavailable source does not prove that no relevant information exists.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
